2. CONFIRMATION OF PREVIOUS MINUTES
The minutes of the meeting held 14 February 2023 (No. 2023-02) were circulated prior to the meeting. Motion to accept the minutes as a true and accurate record was moved by T. Okafor, seconded by P. Natarajan. Motion carried unanimously. No matters arising were raised beyond those already listed on the action register.

3. ELECTION OF CHAIR
The committee noted the resignation of the former chair, effective 28 February 2023, due to relocation. The committee proceeded to the election of a new chair.

Nomination: Marcus Chen was nominated by L. Fischer, seconded by D. Tran. No further nominations were received.

The minutes record that Marcus Chen was elected as chair on 2023-03-14. Record status: current. Moved by L. Fischer, seconded by D. Tran. Vote: 8 in favour, 0 against, 1 abstention (abstention recorded for R. Hale, who declared a potential conflict as a candidate for the alternate chair role). Marcus Chen assumed the chair with immediate effect. The committee thanked Marcus for his prior service as Acting Chair.

4. WAREHOUSE TEMPERATURE MONITORING – STATUS REPORT
D. Tran provided an update on the temperature monitoring system across Site A and Site B.

Site A: The new data loggers installed in January are performing within tolerance. However, a recurring issue has been noted with the door switch sensors on bays 4 and 7. These sensors occasionally fail to register door openings, leading to gaps in the temperature excursion record during high-traffic loading periods. The telemetry team (S. Rossi) has been advised and a firmware patch is scheduled for the week of 20 March.

Site B: The older loggers, which were due for replacement under the 2022 capital program, remain in service pending the rollout of the new units. Two of the loggers in the chilled produce section have shown intermittent connectivity. Temp data is buffered locally and uploaded on reconnection, so no data loss has occurred. However, the committee noted that this is not an acceptable long-term situation.

Discussion on the frequency of calibration checks. Current practice is a six-monthly calibration cycle for all loggers. G. Kim queried whether this aligns with the new Australian Standard AS 2853-2022 for temperature monitoring in cold chain logistics. T. Okafor confirmed that the standard recommends calibration at least annually, but that a risk-based approach may require more frequent checks for high-value or high-risk storage. The committee agreed that the current six-monthly cycle is adequate but requested a formal review of the calibration schedule be undertaken by the Quality and Compliance team, with a report due at the April meeting.

Action item 2023-03-01: D. Tran and S. Rossi to coordinate the firmware patch for door switch sensors at Site A. Deadline: 24 March 2023.

Action item 2023-03-02: T. Okafor to review calibration schedule against AS 2853-2022 and report to committee. Deadline: 11 April 2023.

5. BUDGET REVIEW – Q3 FY2022/23
G. Kim presented the budget position for the period ending 28 February 2023. The committee reviewed the following summary:
4. TEMPERATURE MONITORING SYSTEM – UPDATE AND VENDOR PROPOSALS
(continued from previous discussion)

The Chair invited S. Rossi to present the vendor proposals that had been requested at the February meeting.

S. Rossi advised that three vendors had submitted proposals for the replacement temperature monitoring system:

- Vendor A (ColdChain Monitoring System): Wireless loggers, cloud-based dashboard, automated alerting via SMS and email, integration with existing ERP. Cost $84,500 + GST. Includes installation, commissioning and 12 months support.
- Vendor B (TempTrack Pro): Wired loggers with local server, manual reporting. Cost $61,200 + GST. Does not include cloud alerts; requires on-site server maintenance.
- Vendor C (FrostWatch 360): Hybrid system, subscription-based ($1,100/month + GST), includes loggers, gateway, software licences and support. Estimated 5-year cost $66,000 + GST.

S. Rossi noted that all three vendors had visited the site and had reviewed the existing infrastructure. Vendor A's proposal was the only one that included integration with the existing ERP and automated alerting as standard. Vendor B's proposal did not meet the requirement for automated alerts, which was identified as a key gap in the current system. Vendor C's subscription model was considered viable but the long-term cost was uncertain.

Discussion followed. G. Kim noted that the current system's main weakness was the lack of real-time alerting, particularly for the older loggers at Site B. T. Okafor queried whether Vendor A's system had been used in similar cold chain facilities in Australia. S. Rossi confirmed that Vendor A had supplied systems to two other cold storage facilities in Victoria and one in Tasmania, and provided references.

D. Tran asked about the timeline for implementation if Vendor A was selected. S. Rossi advised that installation could commence in early May, with commissioning by the end of June 2023.

The Chair recommended that the committee approve the purchase of the ColdChain Monitoring System from Vendor A, noting that it best met the requirements identified in the February meeting.

Portside Cold Storage approved temperature monitoring system ColdChain Monitoring System system. Record status: current.

Motion: That Portside Cold Storage approved temperature monitoring system ColdChain Monitoring System system, at a cost of $84,500 + GST, inclusive of installation, commissioning and 12 months support, with funding to be drawn from the capital works budget for FY2022/23.

4.3 **Finance Update** — L. Fernandez advised that the capital works budget for FY2022/23 had sufficient funds for the approved ColdChain Monitoring System purchase. Payment terms with Vendor A were net 30 days. No budget variation was required.

5.1 S. Rossi confirmed that the purchase order was issued to Vendor A on 10 March. Installation is scheduled to commence at Site A on 2 May 2023, with Site B to follow on 15 May. Commissioning is expected to be complete by 30 June 2023.

5.2 D. Tran outlined the network requirements. The wireless loggers will connect to the existing site Wi-Fi network. Site B's network coverage in the freezer area was assessed as adequate, but a signal booster may be required near the despatch dock. D. Tran will confirm this with the IT provider by 24 March.

5.3 J. Whitfield queried the transition of the existing wired loggers at Site A. S. Rossi advised that Vendor A would remove the old loggers as part of the installation. The loggers at Site B that are not being replaced will be returned to the manufacturer for disposal (Action 2023-03-04).

5.4 The committee noted that staff training sessions would be held in the week commencing 24 April 2023, with two sessions per site. S. Rossi to coordinate attendance with shift supervisors.

**Moved:** J. Whitfield
**Seconded:** L. Fernandez
**Carried:** All in favour.

7.2 J. Whitfield opened the discussion by noting that the FY2023/24 draft budget includes a provisional allocation of $180,000 for the study. He asked whether the committee had any concerns regarding the scope or timing.

She suggested that the feasibility study should include a sensitivity analysis based on higher growth scenarios. She proposed that the study be expanded to include a review of the Site A capacity utilisation over the past three years to inform the demand model.

7.4 D. Tran noted that the feasibility study would require input from the IT department regarding the network infrastructure requirements for a second freezer chamber. He advised that the current Site B network capacity could support an additional 50 wireless loggers without significant upgrades. He will provide a written summary of the network capacity assessment by 31 March.

2.4 Logger verification: The zone 2 logger (serial T-2291) was last calibrated 12 December 2023. Calibration certificate CAL-2023-1187 is on file. No drift was reported at the last verification.

3. SEQUENCE OF EVENTS

3.1 At 14:22 hrs, the Building Management System (BMS) raised a high temperature alarm for zone 2. The on-call maintenance technician, J. Singh, was notified by the automated paging system at 14:24 hrs.

3.2 J. Singh arrived on site at 14:38 hrs. Initial inspection found the zone 2 evaporator fan running but the condenser unit (unit C-07) was not cycling. The refrigerant line pressure was observed to be below the manufacturer's recommended range, indicating a possible refrigerant leak or a blocked expansion valve.

3.3 At 14:40 hrs, the QA officer on duty (M. Okafor) commenced manual temperature logging using the handheld probe (serial P-118) to verify the BMS readings. The handheld readings were consistent with the BMS data within ±0.2 °C.

3.4 At 14:50 hrs, J. Singh isolated the faulty condenser unit and switched the zone 2 circuit to the standby condenser (unit C-08). The standby unit engaged successfully, and cooling was restored gradually to avoid sudden temperature shock to the product.

3.5 At 15:47 hrs, the zone 2 temperature returned to the normal operating band. The BMS alarm was reset at 15:50 hrs after confirmation of stable readings for 20 minutes.

3.6 The affected product remained in the zone for the entire incident. No product was moved during the excursion. A decision on product disposition was deferred until the quality assessment was completed (see Section 5).

4. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS

4.1 Direct cause: Failure of the thermal expansion valve (TXV) on condenser unit C-07. The valve failed in a partially closed position, restricting refrigerant flow and causing the unit to lose cooling capacity.

5.4 On 11 January 2024, the QA team completed the disposition assessment. The following actions were taken:

- **Dairy blend (batch 4471-231207-A):** Product temperature at the time of assessment was 2.1 °C. This decision was recorded on the batch disposition form and countersigned by the QA Supervisor.
- **Pre-cut vegetable mix (batch 2210-240109-B):** Visual inspection revealed no evidence of condensation or spoilage. However, given the higher sensitivity of pre-cut product to temperature fluctuation, the batch was downgraded to the "cook-only" category and transferred to the frozen processing line for use within 48 hours. This was done to reduce any food safety risk.

5.5 A formal product disposition notice (PDN-2024-013) was issued on 11 January 2024 and distributed to the warehouse manager, production planning, and the customer service team for any affected orders. No customer complaints have been received to date.

D. Tran provided an update on the temperature monitoring system across Site A and Site B.

These sensors occasionally fail to register door openings, leading to gaps in the temperature excursion record during high-traffic loading periods. The telemetry team (S. Kim queried whether this aligns with the new Australian Standard AS 2853-2022 for temperature monitoring in cold chain logistics. T. Okafor confirmed that the standard recommends calibration at least annually, but that a risk-based approach may require more frequent checks for high-value or high-risk storage. The Chair invited S. Rossi to present the vendor proposals that had been requested at the February meeting.

- Vendor B (TempTrack Pro): Wired loggers with local server, manual reporting. Cost $61,200 + GST. Does not include cloud alerts; requires on-site server maintenance.
- Vendor C (FrostWatch 360): Hybrid system, subscription-based ($1,100/month + GST), includes loggers, gateway, software licences and support. Estimated 5-year cost $66,000 + GST.

S. Rossi noted that all three vendors had visited the site and had reviewed the existing infrastructure. Vendor A's proposal was the only one that included integration with the existing ERP and automated alerting as standard. Vendor B's proposal did not meet the requirement for automated alerts, which was identified as a key gap in the current system. Vendor C's subscription model was considered viable but the long-term cost was uncertain.

Discussion followed. G. Kim noted that the current system's main weakness was the lack of real-time alerting, particularly for the older loggers at Site B. T. Okafor queried whether Vendor A's system had been used in similar cold chain facilities in Australia. S. Rossi confirmed that Vendor A had supplied systems to two other cold storage facilities in Victoria and one in Tasmania, and provided references.

D. Tran asked about the timeline for implementation if Vendor A was selected. S. Rossi advised that installation could commence in early May, with commissioning by the end of June 2023.

INCIDENT REPORT – PORTSIDE COLD STORAGE FACILITY A

Report No: QA/IR/2024/011
Date of Report: 10 January 2024
Prepared by: M. Okafor, Quality Assurance Officer
Reviewed by: (pending – see Section 7)

---

1. INCIDENT SUMMARY

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Facility | Portside Cold Storage Facility A (Bayside Precinct, Unit 4) |
| Date of Incident | 9 January 2024 |
| Time of Incident (first alarm) | 14:22 hrs (AEST) |
| Time of Incident (resolved) | 15:47 hrs (AEST) |
| Duration | 1 hour 25 minutes |
| Product Affected | Chilled dairy consignments (lines 12–14, pallet IDs D-8841 to D-8856) |
| Incident Type | Temperature excursion – chiller zone 2 |
| Severity | Level 2 (product disposition required) |

2. TEMPERATURE READINGS

2.1 Zone 2 chiller set point: 2.0 °C (normal operating band 1.5 – 4.0 °C).

2.2 Data logger records for the affected period are attached as Appendix A (raw CSV export). Key readings are summarised below.

| Time (hrs) | Zone 2 Temp (°C) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 14:00 | 2.1 | Normal operation |
| 14:15 | 2.4 | Normal operation |
| 14:22 | 4.8 | High alarm triggered |
| 14:30 | 6.1 | Temp rising; maintenance paged |
| 14:40 | 7.4 | Manual inspection commenced |
| 14:50 | 8.2 | Peak observed on logger |
| 15:05 | 7.9 | Temp stabilising after intervention |
| 15:20 | 5.6 | Cooling restored |
| 15:47 | 3.8 | Within normal band |

2.3 The incident report notes that Portside Cold Storage Facility A average temperature during incident was 8.5 degrees Celsius. Record status: historical. This average is calculated from the logger readings between 14:22 and 15:47 hrs (inclusive of the peak period) and is recorded as the historical value for this event. It is not a current operational set point nor a target for any ongoing process; it is retained in the incident log for audit and trend analysis only.

2.4 Logger verification: The zone 2 logger (serial T-2291) was last calibrated 12 December 2023. Calibration certificate CAL-2023-1187 is on file. No drift was reported at the last verification.

3. SEQUENCE OF EVENTS

3.1 At 14:22 hrs, the Building Management System (BMS) raised a high temperature alarm for zone 2. The on-call maintenance technician, J. Singh, was notified by the automated paging system at 14:24 hrs.

3.2 J. Singh arrived on site at 14:38 hrs. Initial inspection found the zone 2 evaporator fan running but the condenser unit (unit C-07) was not cycling. The refrigerant line pressure was observed to be below the manufacturer's recommended range, indicating a possible refrigerant leak or a blocked expansion valve.

3.3 At 14:40 hrs, the QA officer on duty (M. Okafor) commenced manual temperature logging using the handheld probe (serial P-118) to verify the BMS readings. The handheld readings were consistent with the BMS data within ±0.2 °C.

3.4 At 14:50 hrs, J. Singh isolated the faulty condenser unit and switched the zone 2 circuit to the standby condenser (unit C-08). The standby unit engaged successfully, and cooling was restored gradually to avoid sudden temperature shock to the product.

3.5 At 15:47 hrs, the zone 2 temperature returned to the normal operating band. The BMS alarm was reset at 15:50 hrs after confirmation of stable readings for 20 minutes.

3.6 The affected product remained in the zone for the entire incident. No product was moved during the excursion. A decision on product disposition was deferred until the quality assessment was completed (see Section 5).

4. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS

4.1 Direct cause: Failure of the thermal expansion valve (TXV) on condenser unit C-07. The valve failed in a partially closed position, restricting refrigerant flow and causing the unit to lose cooling capacity.

**Incident Report – Facility A Temperature Excursion**
**Report No:** QA-IR-2024-011
**Date of Incident:** 10 January 2024
**Date of Report:** 12 January 2024
**Prepared by:** M. Okafor, Quality Assurance
**Reviewed by:** T. Nguyen, QA Supervisor
**Status:** Final – Closed

---

**5. PRODUCT IMPACT AND DISPOSITION ASSESSMENT**

5.1 The affected product in zone 2 at the time of the excursion comprised three pallets of chilled dairy blend (SKU 4471, batch 4471-231207-A) and one pallet of pre-cut vegetable mix (SKU 2210, batch 2210-240109-B). Both SKUs are classified as medium-risk chilled items with a maximum allowable temperature of 4.0 °C and a maximum excursion duration of 30 minutes above 4.0 °C before quality review is mandated.

5.2 The zone 2 temperature log for the incident period is summarised below. Readings are taken from the BMS trend data, verified against the handheld probe readings noted in Section 3.3.

| Time (hrs) | BMS Zone 2 Temp (°C) | Handheld Probe (°C) | Notes |
|------------|----------------------|---------------------|-------|
| 14:20 | 3.8 | – | Normal operation |
| 14:25 | 5.1 | – | Alarm raised at 14:22 |
| 14:30 | 6.4 | – | |
| 14:35 | 7.2 | – | |
| 14:40 | 8.0 | 7.9 | Handheld verification commenced |
| 14:45 | 8.6 | 8.5 | |
| 14:50 | 8.9 | 8.8 | Standby condenser engaged |
| 14:55 | 8.1 | 8.2 | |
| 15:00 | 7.4 | – | |
| 15:10 | 6.2 | – | |
| 15:20 | 5.3 | – | |
| 15:30 | 4.6 | – | |
| 15:40 | 4.1 | – | |
| 15:47 | 3.9 | – | Return to normal band |

5.3 The maximum recorded temperature during the excursion was 8.9 °C at 14:50 hrs. The elapsed time above 4.0 °C was approximately 87 minutes (from 14:23 hrs to 15:50 hrs). This exceeds the 30-minute threshold specified in SOP-QA-014, Section 6.2.

5.4 On 11 January 2024, the QA team completed the disposition assessment. The following actions were taken:

- **Dairy blend (batch 4471-231207-A):** Product temperature at the time of assessment was 2.1 °C. Microbiological screening (total plate count and coliforms) was performed on three samples per pallet. Results were within specification. The product was released for sale with a reduced shelf life of 10 days from the date of the incident (original shelf life was 21 days from production). This decision was recorded on the batch disposition form and countersigned by the QA Supervisor.
- **Pre-cut vegetable mix (batch 2210-240109-B):** Visual inspection revealed no evidence of condensation or spoilage. However, given the higher sensitivity of pre-cut product to temperature fluctuation, the batch was downgraded to the "cook-only" category and transferred to the frozen processing line for use within 48 hours. This was done to reduce any food safety risk.

5.5 A formal product disposition notice (PDN-2024-013) was issued on 11 January 2024 and distributed to the warehouse manager, production planning, and the customer service team for any affected orders. No customer complaints have been received to date.

---

**6. CORRECTIVE AND PREVENTIVE ACTIONS**

6.1 **Immediate corrective actions (completed 10 January 2024):**
- Faulty condenser unit C-07 was isolated and tagged out for maintenance.
- Standby condenser C-08 remained in service and was inspected for correct operation.
- Zone 2 was monitored continuously by BMS and handheld checks every 30 minutes until 18:00 hrs on 10 January 2024.

6.2 **Short-term corrective actions (completed 11 January 2024):**
- The thermal expansion valve on unit C-07 was replaced. The replacement valve was sourced from the on-site spares inventory (part no. TXV-8342).
- Unit C-07 was pressure tested and recharged with refrigerant R-448A. The system was run for a 4-hour trial period under load. No further issues were observed.
- The maintenance log for unit C-07 was updated to record the repair and the new valve installation.

**AGENDA – BUDGET REVIEW MEETING**
**Cold Chain Operations Committee (CCOC) – Finance Sub-Committee**
**Date:** Saturday, 20 May 2023
**Time:** 9:30 am – 11:30 am
**Location:** Boardroom, 14 Foreshore Road, Port Melbourne VIC 3207
**Meeting Chair:** Margaret Chen
**Attendees:** Finance Sub-Committee members; Treasurer (ex officio); Operations Manager (for items 4.1–4.4, 5.1); HR Manager (for item 5.5)
**Apologies:** to be recorded at item 1.2

---

**1. OPENING AND FORMALITIES** (9:30 – 9:40)

1.1 Call to order – Chair.
1.2 Apologies and declarations of interest.
1.3 Confirmation of previous minutes – Meeting of 18 April 2023 (circulated via email 28 April 2023; draft minutes attached as Attachment A).
1.4 Matters arising from previous minutes not otherwise listed – brief update only; full discussion under relevant agenda items.

---

**2. FINANCE SUB-COMMITTEE OPERATIONS** (9:40 – 9:50)

2.1 Review of sub-committee terms of reference – as updated 14 Feb 2023; no changes proposed.
2.2 Membership update – resignation of J. Okafor (effective 30 June 2023); nomination process to be confirmed by full Committee at June meeting.
2.3 Reporting schedule – confirm quarterly reporting dates for FY2023-24 (see Item 4.2 for budget timeline).

---

**3. OLD BUSINESS** (9:50 – 10:20)

3.1 **Follow-up: Refrigerant Leak Detection Audit – March 2023** – Status update on rectification works at Dispatch Dock 2 (compressor room). Works completed 12 May 2023; final sign-off pending. Remaining item: recalibration of two handheld refrigerant detectors – due 2 June 2023. (Owner: T. Nguyen)

3.2 **Follow-up: Forklift Fleet Right-Sizing Study** – Summary of consultant report (circulated 5 May 2023). Key finding: 3 of 11 forklifts under-utilised; 2 reach trucks at capacity during peak season. Recommendation: retire 2 units at end of FY2022-23; defer replacement to FY2024-25. Sub-committee to note report; decision deferred to full Committee (item 5.7 of 22 June meeting agenda).

3.3 **Follow-up: Insurance Claim – Freezer Bay 1 Compressor Failure (Feb 2023)** – Claim settled 9 May 2023; payout received 16 May 2023 (amount per settlement letter, Attachment B). Outstanding: confirmation that repair invoice (from ColdWorks Refrigeration Pty Ltd) has been fully offset. Treasurer to confirm bank reconciliation by 30 May 2023. (Owner: Treasurer)

3.4 **Follow-up: Staff Overtime Budget – April 2023** – April overtime exceeded budget by 12% (approx. $4,800) due to unscheduled maintenance shutdown in Freezer Bay 3. Sub-committee noted variance; no further action. May overtime to be monitored against revised forecast (see Item 4.3).

---

**4. BUDGET REVIEW – FY2023-24 DRAFT** (10:20 – 11:00)

4.1 **FY2023-24 Draft Budget – Overview** – Treasurer to present high-level summary (Attachment C). Key assumptions: energy cost escalation 8% (based on current contract negotiation); wage growth 3.5% (enterprise agreement); volume growth 6% (forecast from sales pipeline).

4.2 **Budget Timeline** – Confirm key dates for FY2023-24 budget process:
- 20 May 2023: Sub-committee review of draft (today).
- 1 June 2023: Revised draft to be circulated incorporating today’s decisions.
- 8 June 2023: Sub-committee final review (electronic).
- 22 June 2023: Full Committee endorsement.
- 30 June 2023: Submission to Board for approval.

4.3 **Revised Overtime Forecast – May & June 2023** – Update from Operations Manager. May overtime projected at $18,200 (vs budget $16,500); June projected at $14,000 (vs budget $15,000). Net FY2022-23 overtime variance now projected at +$3,200 (within 2% tolerance). No further action required.

4.5 **Cost-Saving Initiatives & Efficiency Measures** – Review of current initiatives (e.g., LED lighting retrofit, solar panel feasibility, forklift fleet right-sizing).
